takeaway: A pulmonary artery catheter measures pressures, cardiac output and mixed venous oxygen saturation directly; pulmonary vascular resistance is a derived (calculated) value.

question.text: A pulmonary artery catheter passes through the right heart into the pulmonary artery. Which parameter is not measured directly by it?

lines.text: A pulmonary artery catheter is threaded through the right heart into the pulmonary artery.
It reads some things directly: mean arterial pressure,
cardiac output, and mixed venous oxygen saturation.
The book also lists heart rate and ejection fraction as direct measurements.
Pulmonary vascular resistance is different. The catheter does not read it.
It is calculated from the pressures and the cardiac output.
Other derived values include cardiac index, stroke volume and oxygen delivery.
So the one not measured directly is pulmonary vascular resistance.
